ch32.sub: The Religion about Jesus and the Religion of Jesus
ch32.sum: Christianity was born of the life and teachings of Jesus, yet after Pentecost the gospel of the kingdom was changed into a gospel about the risen Christ. Peter founded the church, Paul shaped its theology, the Greek world received and Hellenized it, and the Roman world paganized and institutionalized it. In the process many of Jesus' ideals were compromised, but they were not lost, and Christianity became one of the greatest powers for good on earth. This chapter traces the formation and transformation of Christianity, its contributions and its handicaps, and arrives at the conclusion that what the world now most needs is, once again, the living Jesus himself. A religion about Jesus may be preached, but the religion of Jesus must be lived.
ch32.s1: From the Gospel of the Kingdom to the Gospel about Christ
ch32.s1.u1.k: After Pentecost the message of Jesus became the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ.
ch32.s1.u1.p: What Jesus entrusted to his apostles was the gospel of the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man. But the minds of the disciples who had experienced the resurrection were filled with Jesus himself, and the center of their proclamation shifted to his life, death, and resurrection and to the hope of his speedy return. The brotherly love of the early communities was truly wonderful, yet it sprang from fellowship among believers in Jesus more than from the recognition that all men are brothers. The shift was a mistake, and at the same time the beginning of the greatest religion mankind had yet known.
ch32.s1.u2.k: Peter founded the church, and Paul transformed the new gospel into Christianity.
ch32.s1.u2.p: The formation of Christianity bears clear names. In the enthusiasm of Pentecost Peter inaugurated the religion of the risen and glorified Christ, and Paul systematized it through his experience on the Damascus road and his own theology, carrying it to the gentile world. Thus the gospel of the kingdom is rooted in the religious experience of the Jesus of Galilee, while Christianity rests chiefly on the religious experience of Paul.
ch32.s1.u3.k: As Christianity became Occidentalized, it began to lose its universal appeal to all races.
ch32.s1.u3.p: Christianity grew on the foundation of Jewish theology, absorbing Zoroastrian teachings and Greek philosophy along the way. In the process it became so thoroughly Occidentalized that to non-European peoples it looked like a strange revelation of a strange God. Christianity glorified Jesus as the Christ but largely forgot his personal gospel, the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of all men.
ch32.s2.u1.k: The Western world had a great culture but hungered for a soul-satisfying religion.
ch32.s2.u1.p: Christianity spread swiftly through the Roman world because of that world's spiritual void. People who had inherited great achievements in philosophy, art, and politics had grown skeptical of every existing religion and philosophy, and the popularity of the mystery cults revealed a deep longing for survival and personal righteousness. The mysteries could not satisfy that longing, but they prepared the way for the reception of Jesus, who brought the bread and the water of life.
ch32.s2.u2.k: Greek philosophy and the teachings of Jesus shared the goal of the emergence of the individual.
ch32.s2.u2.p: The Hellenization of Christianity was not merely a corruption. The Greek taught intellectual liberty and Jesus taught spiritual liberty, and the meeting of the two became a new charter for human freedom. Then Rome, which had an empire but no God, and the Christians, who had a God but no empire, embraced each other. Rome gave the Western world a unity of political rule, Greece a unity of culture, and Christianity a unity of religious thought.
ch32.s2.u3.k: The early leaders compromised Jesus' ideals, yet those ideals remain latent in his gospel.
ch32.s2.u3.p: Compromise with the pagan world brought ritual and pageantry into Christianity. Yet what was gained in exchange was great: a higher standard of human morals, an enlarged concept of God, the hope of immortality as part of a recognized religion, and above all, Jesus of Nazareth given to hungry souls. The compromised ideals were not discarded; they only slumber, and one day they will assert their full power upon the world.
ch32.s3.u1.k: Christianity is an extemporized religion, yet it holds enough of Jesus' teachings to be immortal.
ch32.s3.u1.p: It is easy to point out the defects of Christianity, but the text first asks that it not be lightly regarded. Christianity is the product of the moral genius of God-knowing men of many races across many ages. The teachings set in motion by the ordinary disciples of a crucified carpenter conquered the Roman world and later awoke of themselves from a thousand-year coma. The source of that vitality is the teaching of Jesus still contained within it.
ch32.s3.u2.k: Christianity is handicapped by its identification with the social system of Western civilization.
ch32.s3.u2.p: The greatest difficulty Christianity faces comes not from external enemies but from alliances of its own making. The world sees Christianity as part of the industrial life and moral standards of the West, the apparent sponsor of a society that tolerated science without idealism and power without conscience. The church's entanglement in commerce and politics, and its smothering of newborn faith and persecution of truth bearers in unorthodox dress, are remembered as a betrayal of the Master.
ch32.s3.u3.k: The turbulent history of Christianity shows that it possesses deep powers of recovery.
ch32.s3.u3.p: Hellenization, paganization, secularization, institutionalization, decadence and hibernation, threatened extinction, then rejuvenation and fragmentation: the record of Christianity reads like a catalog of decline, yet the text reads in that very record an inherent vitality. Now Christianity faces a greater test, an age ruled by scientific minds and materialistic tendencies. But the text affirms that in the struggle between the secular and the spiritual, the religion of Jesus will eventually triumph.
ch32.s4.u1.k: The true church is an invisible spiritual brotherhood, marked by unity rather than uniformity.
ch32.s4.u1.p: Jesus did not found the so-called Christian church, but he has fostered it as the best existing exponent of his work on earth. The true church, however, is not a visible organization but the invisible brotherhood of those joined by faith to the living Jesus. The hope of unity for a divided Christendom lies not in doctrinal uniformity but in the living Jesus. Social organizations may serve that brotherhood, but they must never replace it.
ch32.s4.u2.k: Christianity has served the world greatly, but what is now most needed is Jesus.
ch32.s4.u2.p: The renewal of Christianity does not lie in a return to the primitive church; one must go forward from where one stands. What the world needs to see is Jesus living again in the lives of spirit-born men and women. The hope of Christianity is to cease sponsoring Western civilization, to bow humbly before the cross it has so valiantly extolled, and there to learn anew the living gospel of the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man.
ch32.s4.u3.k: The world needs not secondhand religion but firsthand religion.
ch32.s4.u3.p: Beyond the limitation of being a religion about Jesus, Christianity bears another: most people hold their faith secondhand, just as it was handed down by their teachers. As words describing a beautiful thing cannot thrill like the sight of it, so creeds cannot take the place of the experience of knowing God's presence.
ch32.qs1: Is my faith closer to a religion about Jesus or to the religion of Jesus?
ch32.qs2: What attitude in my life would it mean to see the defects of the church without lightly regarding it?
ch32.qs3: What can I do to turn a faith handed down to me into a faith I experience firsthand?
ch33.sub: The Living Experience of Knowing God
ch33.sum: Religion, as The Urantia Book presents it, is neither a system of doctrine nor a mystic ecstasy. It is the living experience of a person who knows God as Father and man as brother. The divine spirit meets man less in feeling than in his highest thinking, and that meeting becomes spiritual insight. Religious experience cannot be bestowed or borrowed; it grows in proportion to the quest for final values, and its driving power is a living faith that governs the way one lives. This chapter considers in turn the nature of religious experience, its growth, the character of faith, and the fruits the experience bears in service and in peace. The reality of religion shows itself more in living than in explanation, and one who has found God lives as if already in the presence of the Eternal.
ch33.s1.u1.k: True religion is to know God as Father and man as brother.
ch33.s1.u1.p: The definition of religion is simple: the personal experience of knowing God as Father, and the realization that naturally follows from it, knowing man as brother. The first is wholly inward, but the second requires a social adjustment of the self to other selves. Religion therefore begins within and moves outward. A belief that leans on threats of punishment or promises of mystical reward is far from this definition.
ch33.s1.u2.k: Religion is not the product of reason, yet viewed from within it is altogether reasonable.
ch33.s1.u2.p: Religion rejects two opposite misunderstandings. One sees it as a philosophic system to be reasoned out and proved by evidence; the other sees it as an indescribable ecstasy enjoyed only by a few mystics. Religion is not the product of reason, yet viewed from within it is altogether reasonable; it is not intellectual assent to doctrine but insight into reality.
ch33.s1.u3.k: It is our thoughts, not our feelings, that lead us Godward.
ch33.s1.u3.p: Contrary to the common view that religion belongs to the realm of emotion, the text says that the divine spirit contacts man in his highest and most spiritualized thinking. This does not belittle feeling. It means that the eye which discerns God is the eye of the mind, and that mind must be pure.
ch33.s2.u1.k: Religion cannot be bestowed or borrowed; it grows as the quest for final values grows.
ch33.s2.u1.p: Religion is not a possession that can be inherited or passed on by instruction. Like all growth of body, mind, and spirit, religious growth happens unconsciously, and no one can force it. But one can supply favorable conditions. Man's only contribution to growth is the mobilization of all the powers of his personality, which is living faith.
ch33.s2.u2.k: Spiritual growth moves from awakening to needs, to discerning meanings, to discovering values.
ch33.s2.u2.p: Spiritual growth has an order. First one awakens to what is lacking, then discerns the meanings of things, and at last discovers what is truly valuable. The evidence of such growth is not the amount of theological knowledge but motives born of love, unselfish ministry, and wholehearted worship of the ideals of divinity. Spirituality thus becomes the measure both of one's nearness to God and of one's usefulness to others.
ch33.s2.u3.k: Emotion alone is false conversion, and mystic states must not be confused with spiritual communion.
ch33.s2.u3.p: Dramatic conversion experiences and mystic ecstasies are easily taken for the summit of religion. The text calmly observes that the very factors which induce such states reveal their danger. States produced by fatigue, fasting, fear, and violent emotion can be dangerous. Feeling must be joined by faith. Jesus' communion with his Adjuster was something quite different from such mystic states.
ch33.s3.u1.p: To accept a teaching as true is still only belief. It becomes faith when it moves life and actually governs the way one lives. Beliefs can be held in common by a group, but faith grows only in the heart of the individual. And faith honors truth, beauty, and goodness without worshiping them; it turns to God alone, who personifies them all.
ch33.s3.u2.k: Genuine spiritual faith is proved by the way it responds amid trial and adversity.
ch33.s3.u2.p: The reality of faith shows itself less on calm days than on hard ones. The text lists the responses of a soul that possesses faith: it advances morality against animal tendencies, trusts the goodness of God in bitter disappointment, finds courage in the face of calamity, and keeps its poise amid illness and pain. These responses, arising where life looks like defeat, reveal the potential divinity of the emerging soul.
ch33.s3.u3.k: Religionists live as if already in the presence of the Eternal.
ch33.s3.u3.p: The elements of religious experience are hard to analyze, but its results are not hard to observe. Believers live today as if immortality were already in their grasp. Religion does not remove human troubles, but it dissolves, illuminates, and transcends them. And faith bridges the gulf between the intellect's logic, which knows the First Cause as It, and the soul's affirmation that the First Cause is He, the heavenly Father.
ch33.s4.u1.k: Religion is not a technique for peace of mind but an impulse that organizes the soul for service.
ch33.s4.u1.p: To treat religion only as a private refuge is to miss its essence. True religion enlists the whole self in the loyal service of loving God and serving man. It takes nothing away from life but adds new meaning to everything and generates fresh enthusiasm and courage. Yet unless that zeal is governed by spiritual insight and faithfulness to ordinary social duties, it can turn into a dangerous crusading spirit.
ch33.s4.u2.k: One who finds God is impelled into loving service to refresh his fellows.
ch33.s4.u2.p: Religious desire is hunger for divine reality, and religious experience is the consciousness of having found God. One who has found God does not seek to boast of it. He simply seeks loving contact with others so that the goodness welling up in his soul may overflow to refresh them. This unselfish interest in others arises because the same God fragment indwells every person. Philosophic uniformity is beyond reach, yet spiritual unity is possible.
ch33.s4.u3.k: A remarkable mark of religious living is a dynamic peace that passes all understanding.
ch33.s4.u3.p: The peace religion gives is not a motionless calm. It is a cosmic poise maintained in the midst of service and adventure, a stability that settles where doubt and turmoil have gone. This peace is immune to disappointment. One who has grasped the reality of the Supreme and pursues the goal of the Ultimate enjoys both the glory of triumph and a deep sense of security.
ch33.qs1: Does my faith remain a belief handed down to me, or is it a faith that actually changes the way I live?
ch33.qs2: When I suffer disappointment or injustice, how does my faith show itself in my response?
ch33.qs3: If the experience of knowing God has ever led me into service to others, what did that look like?
ch34.sub: Two Ways of Communion with the Father
ch34.sum: Prayer and worship are two ways in which man communes personally with God. Prayer is not magic that tries to fit God to man's wishes but a process of fitting the human will to the divine will, and God answers prayer by giving a larger grasp of truth, beauty, and goodness. The prayer of one wholly dedicated to doing the Father's will cannot remain unanswered. Worship goes a step further: it asks nothing and is offered to God simply for what he is, in self-forgetting adoration. This chapter considers the nature and conditions of prayer, the character of worship, and the way in which prayer grows into worship. Prayer enriches the life, while worship illuminates destiny and makes us ever more like the One we worship.
ch34.s1.u1.k: Prayer is the sincere and longing look of the child to its spirit Father.
ch34.s1.u1.p: Jesus taught prayer not as a set formula but as an attitude of the soul. Prayer is the soul's spontaneous expression toward the spirit, the fellowship between a son and his Father. It is the sincere attitude of reaching heavenward for the attainment of one's ideals, a psychological process of exchanging the human will for the divine will. Prayer thus has its place within God's plan for turning what is into what ought to be.
ch34.s1.u2.k: Magic tries to adjust Deity to conditions; prayer adjusts the personality to the will of Deity.
ch34.s1.u2.p: Prayer and magic may look alike, but they point in opposite directions. Magic seeks to move supernatural power to obtain a desired result; prayer seeks to bring oneself into line with the will of God. So prayer does not change God, but it changes the one who prays. In those who have prayed with faith and confident expectation there have grown peace of mind, cheerfulness, courage, self-mastery, and fair-mindedness.
ch34.s1.u3.k: Prayer is not an escape from conflict but a stimulus to growth in the face of conflict.
ch34.s1.u3.p: Prayer does not replace action. A prayer that hands over to God the problem one ought to solve oneself can become a form of sloth. But a prayer asking for wisdom and strength to light and sustain one's way while wrestling with the problem is always right. So the text counsels us to pray for values rather than things, for growth rather than gratification. Prayer is not a way around difficulty but a way of growing through it.
ch34.s2.u1.k: God answers prayer with an enlarged grasp of truth, beauty, and goodness.
ch34.s2.u1.p: The answer to prayer is not the same as receiving exactly what one asked for. As a wise parent does not grant a foolish request but gives the child what is truly needed, so the heavenly Father gives the spirit and many more blessings to those who ask. God's answer comes as a larger revelation of truth, a deeper appreciation of beauty, and a higher concept of goodness. That is why prayer is the most potent stimulus to spiritual growth.
ch34.s2.u2.k: The prayer of one wholly dedicated to doing the Father's will cannot remain unanswered.
ch34.s2.u2.p: There is only one way for every prayer to be answered: that what we ask be wholly in accord with the Father's will. When what the true son desires and what the infinite Father wills become the same, it already is. The five conditions of effective prayer that Jesus taught, unselfishness, faith, sincerity, intelligence, and trust in the Father's all-wise will, all point toward this harmony.
ch34.s2.u3.k: Be fair in prayer; do not expect God to love you more than his other children.
ch34.s2.u3.p: Prayer calls for fairness. A prayer that asks God for favoritism, to love me more than my friends, neighbors, or enemies, is not ethical. Prayer becomes more ethical when it seeks forgiveness and wisdom for self-control. Moreover, deliberately harboring iniquity in the heart gradually cuts off personal communion with God.
ch34.s2.u4.k: Prayer begins with material petition and grows into prayer for one's fellows.
ch34.s2.u4.p: The prayers of childhood, whether of an individual or a race, are selfish and material. Even such prayers have value insofar as they call forth effort, so the mature should be careful not to discourage the prayers of the immature. Yet prayer must grow. Jesus' praying was a remedy for harmful introspection, and he usually prayed in the plural, for his fellows rather than for himself.
ch34.s3.u1.k: Worship is for its own sake; it asks nothing and expects nothing.
ch34.s3.u1.p: The great difference between prayer and worship lies in the presence or absence of self-interest. Prayer contains an element of asking, but true worship contains none. True worship asks nothing for the worshiper and expects nothing in return. Worship is the spontaneous answer of the heart before One who is loved.
ch34.s3.u2.k: Prayer is self-reminding thought; worship is self-forgetting thought.
ch34.s3.u2.p: In prayer a person is still conscious of himself and his needs; in worship he forgets himself. Worship is therefore effortless attention, a restful form of spiritual exertion. In worship the part identifies with the whole, the finite with the Infinite, the son with the Father, time with eternity. Worship is the son's personal communion with the Father, and it refreshes the soul and makes it creative.
ch34.s3.u3.k: The worship experience is the Adjuster's attempt to convey the soul's unutterable longings to the Father.
ch34.s3.u3.p: Worship is not something a person does alone. The indwelling Adjuster seeks to convey to the Father the soul's inexpressible longings, and that soul is the joint creation of the human mind and the Adjuster. That is why a mind of material limitations cannot be fully conscious of the deep meaning of worship. How far one realizes the reality of the worship experience depends not on intellectual level but on the growth of the evolving immortal soul.
ch34.s4.u1.k: Prayer may enrich the life, but worship illuminates destiny.
ch34.s4.u1.p: The text observes that modern religions have overemphasized prayer and neglected the more essential communion of worship. Prayer is not to be abandoned; it is a stairway into worship. Prayer led Jesus' soul into deep communion with the Supreme Rulers of the universe, and it will lead mortals into the communion of true worship. How much of heaven's blessing a person receives depends on the soul's spiritual capacity for receptivity.
ch34.s4.u2.k: Worship makes us increasingly like the One worshiped; it looks to the One to serve the many.
ch34.s4.u2.p: The indwelling spirit speaks best when the human mind is in an attitude of true worship. Worship is a transforming experience that makes us more and more like the One we worship, the way by which the finite gradually approaches the presence of the Infinite. Yet worship is not an escape from the world. We look to the One in order to be inspired to serve the many.
ch34.qs1: Is my praying closer to fitting God to my will, or to fitting my will to God's?
ch34.qs2: Have I experienced worship that asks nothing and is offered to God simply for who he is?
ch34.qs3: How can I make room in my daily life for a time of silent waiting after prayer?
ch35.sum: If the descending Sons come down from above to serve, the ascending sons start from below and climb toward God. Their largest host is the mortals of animal origin, but guardian seraphim, Material Sons, and midwayers also walk this path. Mortals are the last link in the chain of beings called sons of God; they are now faith sons, and they become ascending sons at the moment of fusion with spirit. This chapter considers the classes of ascending sons, the sonship of mortals, the seven stages from planet to Paradise, and the destinies that differ according to the type of fusion, affirming that all these destinies rest under the same love of the Father. Even the faintest desire to find God is enough for any soul to set out on this path.
ch35.s1.u1.k: The story of the ascending sons is a record of divine love and gracious condescension.
ch35.s1.u1.p: The Urantia Book divides beings broadly into descending sons and ascending sons. The ascending sons are revealed in seven classes: Father-fused, Son-fused, and Spirit-fused mortals, evolutionary seraphim, ascending Material Sons, translated midwayers, and Personalized Adjusters. This list is no mere table of categories. The very fact that beings of the lowliest animal origin can rise testifies to the love the Deities pour out without stint on all the universes of time and space.
ch35.s1.u2.k: Not mortals only, but angels and midwayers also share the opportunity of Paradise ascent.
ch35.s1.u2.p: The path of ascent is not open to humans alone. Guardian seraphim attain ascendant sonship through experience and service with ascending mortals, and many join the Mortal Corps of the Finality. Midwayers too, though their Paradise ascent is long deferred, are released from planetary duty once their world reaches the era of light and life. Ascent is a road walked together by very different beings, and service is the key that opens it.
ch35.s2.u1.k: Mortals are the last link in the chain of sons, and the Father draws nearest through the indwelling Adjuster.
ch35.s2.u1.p: The personal touch of the Eternal Son passes down through a series of sons, decreasingly divine and increasingly human, until it reaches a being that man can see and touch. At the end of that chain stand mortals. God the Father does not appear in direct personal form to his countless creatures, but that does not make him distant. The One who is farthest from us in personality draws nearest to us in the indwelling Thought Adjuster, communing with the very soul.
ch35.s2.u2.k: Mortals are not yet of the divine order, yet they are even now faith sons of God.
ch35.s2.u2.p: Mortals are not yet divine by nature; they become ascending sons only upon fusion with an eternal spirit. Yet even before that, man is already a son. The Father has given him personality together with a measure of the divine spontaneity of freewill that God shares with his sons, and a fragment of the Father himself indwells him. Man is therefore even now directly related to the divine Father of all the Sons of God.
ch35.s2.u3.k: Every soul with even the faintest desire to find God will survive.
ch35.s2.u3.p: The secret of survival lies in identification with spirit. Yet the text sets the threshold of survival remarkably low. All that is needed is a willingness to co-operate with the Adjuster and a desire to find God and attain perfection, even if that desire is only the first faint flicker of a primitive grasp of the true light. Survival is not a reward for knowledge or achievement; it depends on the direction of the will toward God.
ch35.s3: The Seven Stages of the Ascending Career
ch35.s3.u1.k: Ascending pilgrims pass through seven stages, from planetary mortals to Paradise arrivals.
ch35.s3.u1.p: The universe career of a mortal is arranged in clear stages. One is born and lives on a planet, rests after death as a sleeping survivor, awakens and learns on the mansion worlds, rises as a morontia progressor, becomes a ward of the superuniverse, passes through Havona as a pilgrim, and arrives at Paradise. The starting point is the same for all: mortals of every world are evolutionary beings of animal origin, and after death they fraternize as one morontia family on the mansion worlds.
ch35.s3.u2.k: In passing from morontia to spirit, mind, personality, and character remain unchanged.
ch35.s3.u2.p: Each stage of the ascent is a continuation, not a break. Morontia progressors rising from the mansion worlds to the local universe headquarters learn by serving on countless assignments with their teachers and senior brethren. Near the time they leave the local universe they acquire true spirit identity, yet this is only a slight transition. The form changes, but mind, personality, and character carry on unchanged. The ascender remains the same person to the end.
ch35.s3.u3.k: To reside on Paradise means that one has found God.
ch35.s3.u3.p: The one who was a creature of flesh and blood on earth becomes a morontia being in the local universe, an evolving spirit in the superuniverse, and receives spiritual education in earnest in Havona. At last he stands on Paradise as a perfected spirit. To dwell there means that one has found God, and those fused with the Father are mustered into the Mortal Corps of the Finality. Yet this arrival is not an end but the beginning of new learning in divinity and absonity.
ch35.s4.u1.k: Because the Father has bestowed himself, he asks ultimate perfection of man.
ch35.s4.u1.p: The command to be perfect flows from the Father's gift. Because the Father has placed his own spirit within man, he can ask for the perfection of becoming one with that spirit. Adjuster-fused mortals are the only class of humans who all traverse the circuits of Havona and find God on Paradise, and before them the career of universal service lies wide open. The text declares that this dignity of destiny and glory of attainment await every one.
ch35.s4.u2.k: Mortal destinies differ, but none is greater or lesser than another.
ch35.s4.u2.p: Destiny differs according to the type of fusion. Spirit-fused mortals generally remain in the local universe, Son-fused survivors in the superuniverse, while Adjuster-fused mortals go on to penetrate the universe of universes, because the fused spirit returns to its level of origin. But the text plainly says not to read these differences as a ranking. The destinies are simply different, and there is no favoritism or arbitrariness in the working of the survival plan.
ch35.s4.u3.k: Sonship is the supreme relationship of the creature to the Creator.
ch35.s4.u3.p: The story of the ascending sons returns in the end to the Father's love. The Father loves each son individually, personally, and irreplaceably, and that love eclipses every other fact, including the differences of destiny. So man can recognize his place in the family of divine sonship and begin to feel the obligation to take up every help the survival plan so freely offers, a plan illuminated by the life of a bestowal Son.
ch35.qs1: How does the fact that my starting point is lowly change my understanding of God's love?
ch35.qs2: How does the teaching that even a faint desire to find God suffices for survival change the way I see other people?
ch35.qs3: If my personality and character continue after death, what kind of character am I cultivating now?
ch36.sub: From the Mansion Worlds to the Threshold of Spirit
ch36.sum: Death is not an end but a door of transition. The survivor who has laid aside the flesh resumes life on the mansion worlds just where death overtook him, awakening as the same person with every worth-while memory. The morontia life is the transition career that lies between matter and spirit, a process of learning what was not learned on earth, correcting defects of character, and growing into universe-mindedness. The Gods do not transform man into a perfected spirit by a single act of magic; they lead him through many stages of gradual change. This chapter considers the continuity beyond death, the education of the mansion worlds, the divine method of gradual change, and the journey toward the threshold of spirit.
ch36.s1.u1.k: Death is a technique of escape from life in the flesh and the entrance to the morontia career.
ch36.s1.u1.p: The Urantia Book pictures death not as a dreadful severance but as a technique: a way of escape from the life of the material flesh, beyond which wait seven worlds of corrective training and cultural education. A survivor awakening on the mansion worlds may notice little difference except a different body. The tabernacle of flesh and blood has been left behind on the world of birth, but life itself goes on unbroken.
ch36.s1.u2.k: The survivor begins over there right where he left off down here.
ch36.s1.u2.p: Between death and resurrection a person gains nothing but the fact of survival. Intellectual training and spiritual development resume at exactly the level where they were interrupted. Death, in other words, does not suddenly make anyone wise or holy. Yet the mansion worlds are also the place where, as a butterfly emerges from the caterpillar, the true personality once hidden in the material flesh is revealed for the first time.
ch36.s1.u3.k: Every memory of survival value is preserved by the Adjuster throughout the ascending career.
ch36.s1.u3.p: To the question whether the survivor is really the same person, the text answers with memory. Purely animal and material associations perish with the brain, but everything worth while and of survival value is counterparted and kept by the Adjuster. The persistence of memory is proof that the original self has been preserved. Thus what was worth while remains part of personal memory throughout the ascendant career.
ch36.s2: Correction and Education on the Mansion Worlds
ch36.s2.u1.k: Almost the entire experience of the first mansion world is deficiency ministry.
ch36.s2.u1.p: Before they are any paradise of reward, the mansion worlds are a school of healing and correction. Survivors from worlds like Urantia arrive with many defects of character and deficiencies of experience, so the chief activities of the first world are devoted to correcting these legacies of the life in the flesh. On the second world intellectual conflicts and mental disharmonies are healed. God's plan receives a person as he is and patiently raises him from there.
ch36.s2.u2.k: The destiny of eternity is determined moment by moment by the achievements of daily living.
ch36.s2.u2.p: The morontia instructor on the first mansion world uses brief statements of human philosophy to help new sojourners grasp the meaning of mota. Several of them remind us that there are no short cuts on the ascending path. The soul is made divine not by what it does but by what it strives to do, and death adds nothing to intellect or spiritual endowment. Since the acts of today are the destiny of tomorrow, postponement can never be avoidance.
ch36.s2.u3.k: A real birth of cosmic consciousness takes place on the fifth mansion world.
ch36.s2.u3.p: The education of the mansion worlds does not stop at correcting defects. On the fifth mansion world a real birth of cosmic consciousness takes place. Now study becomes voluntary rather than required, unselfish service becomes natural, and worship becomes spontaneous. When goodness once practiced with effort becomes second nature, a real morontia character is budding.
ch36.s2.u4.k: Ascenders learn to be faithful, earnest, and cheerful under pressure.
ch36.s2.u4.p: The path of ascent is an earnest struggle, but not a joyless one. The ministers of the mansion worlds teach how to let pressure produce stability, to accept challenges without complaint, and to face difficulties without fear. They ask: if you fail, will you rise to try again? And beings striving upward under sustained stress have the greatest need of humor and relaxation.
ch36.s3.u1.k: The Gods do not change a creature of animal nature into a perfected spirit by a single act of magic.
ch36.s3.u1.p: Many religious traditions imagine that a person becomes a perfected spirit at the moment of death. The text firmly calls such ideas pleasing fables. There can be no magic in the dissolution of the material body that instantly turns a human mind into an immortal spirit. When God wants perfect beings, he creates them so from the beginning. But he never undertakes to convert beings of animal origin into perfection in a single step.
ch36.s3.u2.k: The morontia life begins already on earth, at the moment the soul is conceived.
ch36.s3.u2.p: The morontia life does not begin only after death. The soul is conceived at the moment the Adjuster indwells a mind capable of moral choice, and from then on the morontia career has already begun. In the days of the flesh the divine spirit dwells in man almost as a thing apart, but in the morontia life that spirit becomes a real part of the personality. Through hundreds of gradual transformations a person rises from matter to spirit.
ch36.s3.u3.k: Fusion with the Adjuster follows a final and irrevocable choice for the eternal career.
ch36.s3.u3.p: The most brilliant event of the morontia career is the fusion of the human mind with the divine Adjuster, usually achieved in fact on the fifth or sixth mansion world. Fusion occurs only when it has been pronounced that the human nature has made a final and irrevocable choice for the eternal career. God does not run ahead of human choice. He waits until free choice has matured and then brings about the eternal at-onement.
ch36.s4.u1.k: On the seventh mansion world the differences of origin vanish, and the last remnants of the mark of the beast are removed.
ch36.s4.u1.p: On the seventh mansion world the differences between those from isolated and retarded worlds and those from advanced worlds are virtually erased. The remnants of unfortunate heredity, unwholesome environment, and unspiritual tendencies are all washed away. A disadvantaged starting point does not become an eternal handicap. And when the ascender leaves the system headquarters for Edentia, the personality begun in the flesh is at last fully unified and proclaimed a true child of the Most Highs.
ch36.s4.u2.k: The goal of the survival plan is not endless ease but transcendent service.
ch36.s4.u2.p: The morontia career is the evolutionary portal to spirit life, leading on to the goal of time, the finding of God on Paradise. Yet the purpose of all this labor and training is not merely that man should survive to enjoy endless bliss. God's purpose in making the whole universe one vast training school is to prepare man for a transcendent service hidden beyond the horizon of the present universe age.
ch36.qs1: If after death I begin again right where I left off, where am I standing now?
ch36.qs2: How might I correct here and now habits such as procrastination and avoidance that must otherwise be rooted out on the mansion worlds?
ch36.qs3: How does knowing that gradual growth, not sudden change, is God's method help me view my own slow progress?
ch37.sub: The Paradise Destiny of Ascending Mortals
ch37.sum: Ascending mortals who reach Paradise and find God are mustered into the Corps of Mortal Finaliters. Around the core of Father-fused mortals the corps includes glorified seraphim, Havona natives, midwayers, Material Sons, and Gravity Messengers, all received as equals without losing their individuality. Yet arrival is not the end. The finaliters now return to serve in the universes of time, undergoing what may be called postgraduate training in universe administration. This chapter considers the composition of the corps, its present mission, the mobilization of the seven corps of finality, and what their unrevealed destiny in the universes of outer space may imply.
ch37.s1.u1.k: The Corps of Mortal Finaliters is the present known destination of Adjuster-fused mortals.
ch37.s1.u1.p: At the end of the long ascent, mortals arrive at the Corps of the Finality. The corps is made up of six groups: Havona natives, Gravity Messengers, glorified mortals, adopted seraphim, and glorified Material Sons and midway creatures. They now minister to the universes of space and administer worlds settled in light and life, but the text cautiously conjectures that their future destination is the universes of outer space now being organized.
ch37.s1.u2.k: The finaliters embrace both the perfect and the perfected.
ch37.s1.u2.p: The beauty of this corps lies in the meeting of very different beings. Havona natives, perfect beings of direct creation, bring to the corps the viewpoint of one born in perfection. Many guardian seraphim who have watched over mortals ascend with their wards, take the finaliter oath, and forever accept the destiny of their mortal companions. Those perfect from the beginning and those perfected through experience form a single body.
ch37.s1.u3.k: All finaliters are received as equals, yet that equality never erases individuality.
ch37.s1.u3.p: The corps is organized according to working associations on the worlds of space and the experience accumulated through the long ascendant career. Most of its members are ascendant mortals, and in each company of a thousand there are only ten places for those who are neither mortal nor seraphic. All are received as equals, yet that exalted equality never abolishes individuality or personal identity. The principle that unity is not uniformity holds even on Paradise.
ch37.s2: The Present Mission of Perfected Mortals
ch37.s2.u1.k: Mortal finaliters have found God, yet they have not reached final destiny.
ch37.s2.u1.p: The finaliters are those who have fully complied with the injunction of the ages, "Be you perfect." They have found God and reached the present limit of creature perfection. But the text carefully adds that this is not the finality of ultimate spirit status or of service. The finaliters stand only at the limit now attainable; the farther road of spirit attainment, of service, and of Deity experience still lies open before them.
ch37.s2.u2.k: Finaliters return to serve in the universes of time, and some are always present on Urantia.
ch37.s2.u2.p: Ascenders who reach Paradise do not settle there to rest. The finaliters return to the universes of time, serving in one superuniverse after another and receiving assignment to their native superuniverse only after serving in all six others. In this way they acquire a sevenfold understanding of the Supreme Being. The text says that companies of mortal finaliters are always serving on Urantia. Those who went before are even now at work beside those who follow.
ch37.s2.u3.k: Why are the Gods so concerned to train surviving mortals so thoroughly in universe management?
ch37.s2.u3.p: The present assignments of the finaliters look like postgraduate courses in universe understanding and superuniverse administration. A natural question follows: what is all this training for? It adds that even without any future destiny the present assignment would fully justify the plan of ascent, yet it foresees that future ages in outer space will reveal the wisdom and loving-kindness of the Gods still more fully.
ch37.s3: The Seven Corps of Finality and the Outer Universes
ch37.s3.u1.k: The mobilization of the seven finaliter corps is the grand universe's divinity response to outer space.
ch37.s3.u1.p: The Corps of Mortal Finaliters is not alone. Seven corps of finality are assembling on Paradise, among them the Corps of the Unrevealed Sons of Destiny. The text sees this mobilization as the activity of the Ultimate Trinity preparing for inconceivable developments in outer space. The universe is now preparing for the next age.
ch37.s3.u2.k: The assembling finaliters are destined for future service in the universes of outer space.
ch37.s3.u2.p: The revelators frankly admit that they do not know the plans for the outer creations. Yet of some things they are certain: vast new universes are being organized in outer space, and the mysterious mobilization of perfected ascenders has gone on for ages upon ages. Placing these two movements side by side, it is natural to conjecture that the finaliters will serve in the outer universes, where aggregations of matter larger than any present superuniverse are gathering.
ch37.s3.u3.k: We evolve in the Supreme, and he evolves in us.
ch37.s3.u3.p: The outer universes will be magnificent, yet they will lack one thing: the participation of ascending beings, through finite experience, in the evolution of the Supreme Being. We now suffer many difficulties because the sovereignty of God the Supreme is not yet complete, but for that very reason we share the unique experience of his evolution. The incompleteness of the present age is a deprivation, and at the same time a privilege that will not come again.
ch37.s4.u1.k: The seventh place in the corps of finality is still vacant.
ch37.s4.u1.p: Every finaliter company has a place not yet filled. There are now only six classes of permanent members, and not even the finaliters know who their seventh comrade will be. It may be a being originating in the outer universes, or a Paradise personality not yet created. This vacant place is a sign that theology does not explain everything. Even at the end of the ascent there remain an open future and a waiting.
ch37.s4.u2.k: Partnerships of Creator and creature will become the sympathetic rulers of future universes.
ch37.s4.u2.p: The Adjuster, the highest known manifestation of the First Source and Center, and man, the lowest form of intelligent life able to know the Father, are fused into one. The text calls this mysterious union a wonderful adventure and romance. The text foresees these children of the Supreme, so united, administering a gigantic creation. Having started from the lowest place and passed through every stage by experience, they can understand and sympathize with those they govern. A lowly origin turns out to be a qualification.
ch37.s4.u3.k: What a glorious destiny for the animal-origin children of time.
ch37.s4.u3.p: Born on a planet, passing through the morontia worlds, ascending the spirit universes, traversing Havona, finding God, and attaining Paradise: the text calls this a glorious destiny for the animal-origin children of time. Man's frame is dust, yet if he truly wills and desires it, the heritage of the ages is his. The theology of the Corps of the Finality is, in the end, God's invitation extended to the human will.
ch37.qs1: How does the teaching that endless service awaits even after finding God change my idea of salvation?
ch37.qs2: What comfort and what responsibility does it give me that those who went before are still serving in this world?
ch37.qs3: If my lowly beginnings and present difficulties may one day qualify me to understand and serve others, how shall I regard today's trials?
